title: Flipkart Enters Food Delivery With Low Commissions, Targeting Zomato-Swiggy Duopoly
excerpt: Walmart-backed Flipkart plans a Bengaluru pilot with restaurant commissions as low as 10%, far below the 25-35% charged by incumbents, as India's $9 billion food delivery market heats up.
body:
• Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy confirmed the company will launch food delivery "in the next few weeks," with a pilot expected in Bengaluru by mid-August
  • The company is reportedly considering restaurant commissions of around 10%, roughly a third of the 25-35% charged by Zomato and Swiggy
  • Swiggy shares fell 7% and Eternal (Zomato) dropped 3.4% on July 24 after the announcement, reflecting investor anxiety over the duopoly's future

Flipkart is preparing to enter India's food delivery market within weeks, marking the most serious challenge yet to the Zomato-Swiggy duopoly that has dominated the space for years.

Speaking to Moneycontrol on July 24, Flipkart Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy confirmed the plans. "We will launch food delivery in the next few weeks," he said. "Like everything else we do, we will launch food delivery first, test the value proposition with customers, take feedback and continue improving the product until it really appeals to the customer. After that, we'll start scaling it."

Context

The Walmart-owned e-commerce giant is expected to begin with a limited pilot in Bengaluru, likely around mid-August, before expanding to other cities. According to reports from Business Standard and others, Flipkart is considering restaurant commissions of around 10-11% — a fraction of the 25-35% that Zomato and Swiggy currently charge partners.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=4I00C_0746s

The service will be available through both a standalone app and the existing Flipkart app, with initial rollout expected via the government-backed Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC). Krishnamurthy did not reveal the branding or confirm the launch city, though multiple reports point to Bengaluru.

This is not Flipkart's first attempt at food delivery. The company explored entering through ONDC about two years ago, but those plans did not materialise. The difference this time: Flipkart now operates Flipkart Minutes, its quick commerce arm with over 1,000 dark stores, giving it an established logistics backbone and delivery fleet.

"Before Covid-19, food delivery was just 10% of a restaurant's business. Today, it is the heart of the business, and when your heart of the business becomes 50%, we had never done the pricing where a 20% commission was factored in."

— Sagar Daryani, NRAI President and Wow! Momo Co-founder

Impact

The announcement alone rattled markets. Swiggy shares fell as much as 7% on July 24, while Eternal, Zomato's parent company, dropped over 3.4%, according to Informist Media. Flipkart had not yet launched anything or taken a single customer — investors were reacting purely to the prospect of a well-capitalised newcomer disrupting settled economics.

India's online food delivery market, estimated at $9 billion in FY25, is projected to reach $24-25 billion by FY30, according to Jefferies. Zomato currently commands roughly 57% market share, with Swiggy holding the remaining 43%. Both platforms charge take rates of 21-24%, among the highest globally — well above China's Meituan at 16%.

Flipkart brings formidable assets: approximately 85 million daily active users, Walmart's deep pockets, and the Ekart logistics network. The company's approach mirrors its Flipkart Minutes playbook — start small in one city, learn, then scale aggressively.

Flipkart is also entering at a moment when restaurant owners are pushing back hard. The National Restaurant Association of India (NRAI) has become increasingly vocal about commission structures, with Bengaluru restaurants setting an August 15 deadline for Swiggy to address their grievances, Inc42 reported. Rapido's zero-commission food delivery platform Ownly, which launched in Bengaluru in March, claims to have captured nearly 10% of the city's online food delivery market.

What's Next

The Bengaluru pilot will be the critical test. Watch for how quickly Flipkart expands beyond the first city, how aggressively it uses discounts to acquire customers, and whether the low-commission model attracts enough restaurant partners to build a compelling catalogue.

Krishnamurthy has said Flipkart would enter the category only if it believed it could offer something genuinely different. "We aim to innovate not only on pricing but also on selection, service, reliability and the overall customer experience," he told Moneycontrol.

For Indians ordering food abroad through family or keeping tabs on Indian tech, the implications are clear: this could reshape how restaurants price delivery meals and push Zomato and Swiggy to finally lower their fees. A broader rollout, if the pilot succeeds, is expected between late 2026 and early 2027.
nri_angle: Flipkart's low-commission entry could reshape food delivery pricing across India, affecting how diaspora families order food back home and signaling cheaper delivery for everyone.
author: Diaspora Desk
